page: Vultr voc-m-8c-64gb-400s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark data indicates a strong memory subsystem, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Large-block read-only and write memory bandwidth tests both place in the top 25%. In terms of processing, single-core stress-ng performance is in the top 10%, while multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall within the average range. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show strong performance, though multi-threaded decompression and database operations align with average tier results. Large-model LLM prompt processing represents a bottleneck, registering in the bottom 25% for a medium 7B model.

This server provides a balanced profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. The high memory density relative to the vCPU count offers qualitative cost efficiency for applications requiring large in-memory datasets without the overhead of paying for excess compute cores. It is suitable for memory-cached databases, medium-scale web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring dedicated CPU resources and fast local NVMe storage.
